query:
Someone in the group expressed strong enthusiasm for galaxy season and revealed a specific multi-hour integration plan for a galaxy pair. Who was that person?

Options:
A. Tomás
B. Marcus
C. Jerome
D. Cecilia
context:
[1] (about=Jerome, episodic, t0 @2026-01-09T20:47:00) galaxy season starts in earnest from February so I'll be pulling data on the Leo Triplet first chance the sky opens up. I've got a 10-hour integration plan for M65 and M66 that I've been sitting on since November.
[2] (about=Tomás, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:07:00) Jerome what happened to the M65/M66 project mate? you were so hyped about that back in January 🌌
[3] (about=Jerome, episodic, t4 @2026-03-06T19:55:00) February was a loss for galaxies. I pulled 12 hours across six nights and the transparency killed the faint outer arms every single time. I'm done chasing galaxy targets for this season. Cecilia's nebula images from the 17th actually looked reasonable and I've been reconsidering the target strategy. Emission nebulae don't care about transparency in the same way. The Ha bandpass cuts through almost anything.
[4] (about=Jerome, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:06:00) I will be imaging the Rosette and the Cone Nebula Ha data on the 11th regardless. galaxy season is effectively over for me this year. the transparency variance in this region is simply not compatible with high SNR galaxy work. emission nebulae are a more rational target choice at this latitude.
[5] (about=Jerome, episodic, t6 @2026-04-03T20:08:00) it stalled. 12 hours integration and the tidal bridge between M65 and M66 was not recoverable from the noise floor. I've shelved it. narrowband emission work gives me consistent results. the Rosette at 20 hours Ha will be a significantly better image than anything I'd pull from that galaxy pair.
[6] (about=Jerome, episodic, t2 @2026-02-06T20:20:00) January was a write-off. Three nights I queued up the M66 project and every time transparency dropped below 4 before 11pm. I lost maybe 8 hours of potential integration. Genuinely considering whether galaxies are worth the heartbreak this latitude gives you.
[7] (about=Harriet, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:26:00) This is exactly the episode I want to make. The group as a portrait. Nadia and Ruth as the founders, each of you arriving at a different moment for a different reason. Tomás because of the landscape photography crossover. Marcus because his kids gave him a telescope as a joke. Me because I came to write about it and could not leave. There is a book in this, not just an episode.
[8] (about=Tomás, episodic, t0 @2026-01-09T20:48:00) nice one, I always love galaxy season, even on the wide field you can get Virgo cluster in frame which looks amazin 📸🌌 I'll try grab some landscape foreground with it
[9] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-06-05T20:38:00) dev and I stayed up till 3am watching jupiter and saturn transit. the seeing came up to 4/5 around 1am and at 400x on jupiter you could see three festoons in the NEB simultaneously. that's the best planetary night I've had in two years
[10] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-08-07T20:22:00) Ruth and I met at the county natural-history society in 2021 and discovered within about twenty minutes that we both preferred the stars to anything else on the programme. We agreed to meet the following Friday with our own telescopes in my back garden. There were two of us, a 4-inch refractor, Ruth's old 80mm, and a thermos of tea. I remember we stayed out until 2am on a school night and neither of us could see the point of going in. It grew from there one person at a time. In my experience the quiet beginning is the only honest beginning a group like this can have.
agent_answer:
The person was **Jerome** (Option C).

In the raw excerpts, Jerome said: *"galaxy season starts in earnest from February so I'll be pulling data on the Leo Triplet first chance the sky opens up. I've got a 10-hour integration plan for M65 and M66 that I've been sitting on since November"* — expressing strong enthusiasm for galaxy season and revealing a specific multi-hour integration plan for the M65/M66 galaxy pair.

Tomás expressed general love for galaxy season but gave no multi-hour integration plan for a galaxy pair; Marcus discussed a planetary night; Cecilia appears only in passing reference regarding nebula images.

query:
While Jerome was walking Cecilia through a PixInsight Ha-RGB blending workflow, someone in the chat acknowledged following the walkthrough closely but explicitly positioned themselves as outside the narrowband-PixInsight process. Who was that person?

Options:
A. Dev
B. Ruth
C. Marcus
D. Tomás
context:
[1] (about=Ruth, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:37:00) I cannot speak to the technical aspects but the image looks beautiful. Is it possible that what you have both done this evening is exactly the kind of collaboration that makes this group worth belonging to?
[2] (about=Dev, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:41:00) is that a dumb question but... if I wanted to learn PixInsight where would I even start? lowkey the walkthrough Jerome just did made more sense to me than any YouTube video I've tried
[3] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:32:00) Jerome I just ran the PixelMath blend on the Orion stack and I am SHAKING. The HII emission structure around the running man nebula that I have never been able to pull out is RIGHT THERE. I had completely written off narrowband blending as too technical for me and too cold-looking. This is totally different from what I imagined, the broadband colours are intact and the Ha just adds this incredible red-gold depth to the emission zones!!! I genuinely thought I hated narrowband because it looked monochromatic but you've just shown me I was wrong about the whole thing!!! 😍🌟📷
[4] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t11 @2026-07-10T20:05:00) @all I've been going back and reprocessing my Orion image from November for the hundredth time and it still looks flat compared to Jerome's work. Jerome, I know you've helped me before with the background extraction issue but I think there's something deeper I'm missing with how Ha data could work. Is there any chance you'd walk me through how you actually blend it?? 🙏📷
[5] (about=Cecilia, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:09:00) ok sending the FITS now. and I have to ask... I always thought narrowband looked really cold and mono, like it strips all the warmth out. is there a way to keep the broadband colour and just add the Ha detail on top? 📷
[6] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:14:00) technically speaking the DSLR does not have separate Ha data to blend. you are working with a one-shot colour sensor. the workflow I described requires two separate captures. it is not that I would not help you, it is that the method does not apply to your setup.
[7] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:11:00) that is exactly what the Ha-RGB blend does. you keep the full broadband RGB as your colour base and add the Ha emission only where it contributes signal. the PixInsight workflow I use is: LinearFit both datasets to match background levels, then use PixelMath with the expression: Ha_weight multiplied by Ha plus open-bracket 1 minus Ha_weight close-bracket multiplied by R, where Ha_weight is typically 0.7. you replace the red channel with this blended value and recombine. the result is your broadband warmth with Ha emission boosting the ionised hydrogen regions. it is the best of both methods technically speaking. try it on the Orion core and tell me if the Trapezium halo structure changes.
[8] (about=Jerome, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:07:00) the Ha-RGB blend is not complicated once you understand what you are doing, but there are three things most people get wrong that kill the result. first: your Ha data needs to be calibrated and stacked separately, not mixed in during the initial integration. second: in PixInsight you use the ChannelCombination process with Ha mapped to the red channel of a synthetic luminance, then combine with a Luminance mask to protect star colours. third, and this is where most broadband imagers fail: you need to apply a Hue-Saturation adjustment after the blend to desaturate the magenta cast that appears in the red-blue transition zones around HII regions. if you skip that step your stars look radioactive and the nebula looks like a bad Instagram filter. send me your Orion FITS stack and I will step through it with you here in the chat.
[9] (about=Tomás, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:48:00) right once the HEQ5 is running and I've got first light sorted, I want to get to the point where I can do what Cecilia just did. not there yet but that's the direction mate 🌌✨
[10] (about=Tomás, episodic, t12 @2026-07-10T20:18:00) starting with the 200mm telephoto so I know the camera side already, then saving for a proper fast refractor. baby steps mate 🔭✨
agent_answer:
The person was **A. Dev**.

Dev said: *“lowkey the walkthrough Jerome just did made more sense to me than any YouTube video I've tried”* — acknowledging following the walkthrough closely — while also asking *“if I wanted to learn PixInsight where would I even start?”*, positioning themselves as outside the narrowband/PixInsight process.

The others don’t match: Ruth disclaimed technical knowledge, Cecilia was the one being walked through the process, and Tomás said he wants to get to that point but didn’t say he’d followed the walkthrough closely.
